title: Machine-Checked Exact Combinatorial Certificates for Input-Oblivious Unambiguous Hierarchies, Krentel Lex-Max OGTD Collapse, and Single-Query Promise Elimination
abstract: Edward A. Hirsch (arXiv:2611.33126, November 24, 2026) established sharp structural collapses for input-oblivious unambiguous hierarchies built over OUP, proving that OUH subseteq P^{TALLY cap NP} subseteq P_||^{ONP} (Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2), that OUH^bullet subseteq OGTD[NP] = OUGTD[FP^{ONP}, co-ONP, P] subseteq OUM via Krentel lexicographically-largest transcripts (Lemma 3.1, Theorem 5.1), that the oblivious unambiguous dot-operator hierarchy collapses completely to exists^{ou}.co-OUP = OUP U co-OUP (Theorem 6.2, Corollary 6.3), that a single loose prOUP query reduces to a standard OUP query (OUP^{prOUP[1]} = OUP^{OUP[1]}, Lemma 6.4, Theorem 6.5), and that SOUP = OUP cap co-OUP (Proposition 6.6). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and finite combinatorial certificate auditor for the order-theoretic, pigeonhole, and oracle-consistency core of these results. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (ObliviousUnambiguousHierarchy.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 11 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes Cantor pairing injectivity and upper bounds, inductive tally-census uniqueness, oblivious bit-by-bit witness extraction, Krentel lex-max transcript soundness, inductive ONP prefix-search bit recovery, co-ONP unique testing, fixed-pair refutation and dot-operator collapse soundness, single-loose-query in-promise forcing, and SOUP shared-witness tagging. OUH-CERT-1.0 audits four exact finite modes across 16 canonical certificates (0.038-0.789 ms) and rejects 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
